verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena paccanīkasāto nāma brāhmaṇo sāvatthiyaṁ paṭivasati.
verses.english: Now at that time a brahmin named Contraphile, who loved contradiction, was residing in Sāvatthī.
“Why don’t I go to the ascetic Gotama and

verses.pali: Yaṁ yadeva samaṇo gotamo bhāsissati taṁ tadevassāhaṁ paccanīkāssan”ti.
Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā abbhokāse caṅkamati.
verses.english: At that time the Buddha was walking mindfully in the open air.

verses.pali: Atha kho paccanīkasāto brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ caṅkamantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the brahmin Contraphile went up to the Buddha, and said to him as he was walking,
and you’ve got rid of resentment,

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, paccanīkasāto brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he had spoken, the brahmin Contraphile said to the Buddha,

verses.pali: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
